# NativeLink Metrics Dashboard
Monitor remote execution performance

panels.title: Executions (5m)
panels.description: Counted from the hub's stage-transition counter, which is accurate. Upstream built this panel on a per-action counter that stops labelling after 2,000 distinct action/worker pairs and then reads as zero.

panels.title: Actions not killed (%)
panels.description: Share of actions that ran to the end, as opposed to being killed by a time limit or from outside. It does not say whether the command itself exited successfully: a failing test or compile still counts as ran to the end. The hub's metrics cannot report exit-code failures reliably (see the note on the other panels).

panels.title: Hub uptime
panels.description: Time since the hub's current process started (systemd user unit nativelink-macos-hub.service). Red under 1 h: it restarted recently.

panels.title: Hub restarts (24h)
panels.description: Times the hub process was (re)started in the last 24 h, from the start-time metric. Counts systemd automatic restarts (e.g. after an OOM kill) and manual restarts. History starts 2026-11-21 23:43 PST.

panels.title: OOM kills on headcrash (24h)
panels.description: Kernel OOM kills on the hub host in the last 24 h (any process, not only the hub). History starts 2026-11-21 22:28 PST.

panels.title: Hub unit state
panels.description: Whether systemd reports the hub unit active.

panels.title: Execution Completion Rate
panels.description: Counted from the hub's stage-transition counter, which is accurate. Upstream built this panel on a per-action counter that stops labelling after 2,000 distinct action/worker pairs and then reads as zero.

panels.title: Completed actions since the hub started
panels.description: Counted from the hub's stage-transition counter, which is accurate. Upstream built this panel on a per-action counter that stops labelling after 2,000 distinct action/worker pairs and then reads as zero. Includes actions whose command exited non-zero.

panels.title: Completed and killed actions over time
panels.description: Counted from the hub's stage-transition counter, which is accurate. Upstream built this panel on a per-action counter that stops labelling after 2,000 distinct action/worker pairs and then reads as zero.

panels.title: Killed actions (1h)
panels.description: Actions a worker killed in the last hour: for exceeding a time limit, or stopped from outside (for example when a worker was restarted).

panels.title: Cache size
panels.description: Bytes in use on the volume that holds the hub's stores (CAS and action cache). Nothing else is on that volume.

panels.title: Share of cap used
panels.description: The hub evicts the least recently used entries once the CAS reaches its cap. See the Cache eviction row for eviction volume and how long entries survive.

panels.title: Action cache hit rate (5m)
panels.description: Share of action-cache lookups that found a stored result, so the action did not have to run. A lookup that finds nothing is a miss.

panels.title: Cache growth per hour
panels.description: Net change over the last 30 minutes, scaled to an hour. It falls to zero once the cache sits at its cap and evicts as fast as it fills.

panels.title: Files in cache
panels.description: Files on the store volume: roughly the number of cache entries.

panels.title: Cache size over time
panels.description: The hub evicts the least recently used entries once the CAS reaches its cap. See the Cache eviction row for eviction volume and how long entries survive.

panels.title: Cache requests per second
panels.description: Requests to the content store. Rejected uploads are ones the hub refused, for example because the content no longer matched its digest.

panels.title: CAS fill
panels.description: Bytes in the CAS (sum of entry sizes) as a share of the cap the running hub evicts at. The action cache is not included. At about 100% every write evicts the least recently used entries. Measured by worker-slots-exporter.py (inotify on the hub's CAS directories; see its comments).

panels.title: Oldest cached entry
panels.description: How long an entry nobody touches survives in the CAS: now minus the median last-access time (atime) of the last 1000 entries evicted, i.e. the LRU frontier. It keeps rising while nothing is evicted. A cached action result is served only while all its outputs are still in the CAS, so this is roughly how long a cached test result stays usable. Red under 24 h. Measured by worker-slots-exporter.py (inotify on the hub's CAS directories; see its comments).

panels.title: Evicted in the last hour
panels.description: Bytes and entries the hub evicted from the CAS in the last hour. Measured by worker-slots-exporter.py (inotify on the hub's CAS directories; see its comments).

panels.title: Evicted (bytes/h)
panels.description: Bytes evicted from the CAS per hour (5 min rate), with bytes written for comparison: at the cap the two match. Measured by worker-slots-exporter.py (inotify on the hub's CAS directories; see its comments).

panels.title: Evicted entries/h
panels.description: Entries evicted from the CAS per hour (5 min rate), with entries written for comparison. Measured by worker-slots-exporter.py (inotify on the hub's CAS directories; see its comments).

panels.title: CAS write rate
panels.description: Bytes written into the CAS per second (new entries renamed into the store, 5 min rate). At the cap, the CAS turns over once every cap / write rate. Measured by worker-slots-exporter.py (inotify on the hub's CAS directories; see its comments).

panels.title: Cache retention over time
panels.description: Oldest cached entry: now minus the median atime of the last 1000 evicted entries. Lifetime: median time from write to eviction of those entries. Oldest atime on disk (from a walk every 15 min) overstates retention: the hub's LRU also promotes entries on existence checks, which do not update atime, so a few old files linger. Measured by worker-slots-exporter.py (inotify on the hub's CAS directories; see its comments).

panels.title: Hub /status probe
panels.description: Loopback /status health probe from worker-slots-exporter.py (15 s interval). NativeLink returns 503 whenever FilesystemStore::check_health stat (>2 s) times out.

panels.title: Connected workers
panels.description: Workers connected to MAIN_SCHEDULER from the hub admin API (expected pool size: 10 — 6 macOS + 4 Linux).

panels.title: Store health timeouts (24h)
panels.description: FilesystemStore::check_health stat timeouts logged by the hub in the last 24 h (baseline: 0/day).

panels.title: Hub /status probe latency & failures
panels.description: Loopback /status probe wall latency (seconds; FilesystemStore::check_health times out at 2 s) and non-200 probe counts (5m increase).

panels.title: Connected workers over time
panels.description: Total connected workers (admin API and hub OTel), expected pool size (NL_HEALTH_EXPECTED_WORKERS), and breakdown by OSFamily.

panels.title: Store health timeouts, evictions & decoded-size errors (15m)
panels.description: Hub journal counters (15m increase): FilesystemStore::check_health stat timeouts, worker kill-ack and silence evictions, and compressed-upload decoded-size errors.

panels.title: Action timeouts & kills (15m)
panels.description: Hub journal counters (15m increase): scheduler Action.timeouts ('Timing out operation'), worker command timeouts ('Command timed out on the worker'), and 'Action ended by a kill'.

panels.title: /mnt/cache used (%)
panels.description: Filesystem usage of /mnt/cache (nvme1n1p1) alongside the configured CAS eviction cap (NL_HUB_CAS_MAX_BYTES, ~94.9%). Alert threshold: 96%.

panels.title: nvme1n1 busy (%) & await (ms)
panels.description: I/O completion latency (write/read await in ms, left axis) and busy percentage (right axis) for nvme1n1 backing /mnt/cache on headcrash (1m rate from node_exporter).

panels.title: Host IO pressure (headcrash)
panels.description: Linux PSI IO pressure on headcrash (1m rate from node_exporter): 'some' (at least one task stalled) and 'full' (all non-idle tasks stalled).

panels.title: Host swap & hub memory (headcrash)
panels.description: Host swap usage (node_exporter) and hub cgroup memory (nativelink-macos-hub.service, hub-textfile-metrics.sh). The hub has MemorySwapMax=0; swap reflects the co-located Linux worker and host load.
